questions.prompt: What was the new source of power?
questions.passage: During the 1920's, electric power became more readily available and cheaper in many parts of the world. As a result, many manually operated gadgets were adapted to this new source of power.
questions.markingGuide: Accept electric power or electricity. The passage says gadgets were adapted to this new source of power after electric power became available.

questions.prompt: What was William Harvey's great discovery?
questions.passage: In the 1600's William Harvey made a great discovery. Up until this time, it was thought that blood flowed back and forth inside our bodies like the tide. Instead, he found that it flows around the body.
questions.expectedAnswer: That blood flows around the body (circulates)
questions.markingGuide: Accept that blood flows / circulates around the body (not back and forth like the tide).

questions.prompt: Who said they couldn't afford it?
questions.passage:
I wouldn't mind one of those, said Nigel with envy.

We couldn't afford it, came the reply.

They were looking at PJ's new sports car. Dawn went back to the gardening but Nigel kept looking.
questions.markingGuide: Accept Dawn. Nigel spoke first with envy; the reply came from Dawn, who then went back to gardening while Nigel kept looking.

questions.prompt: Who said 'In the town square then'?
questions.passage:
We'll meet outside the library, said Greta.

No, not there, exclaimed Anna. It's too far away. What about the bus station?

It's dark and creepy at night, said Greta.

In the town square then?

That's a good idea. On Friday nights there's a lot of people in the square.
questions.markingGuide: Accept Anna. Greta's lines are labelled. Anna rejects the library and suggests the bus station; after Greta rejects that, the next suggestion ('In the town square then?') continues Anna's turn. Greta then agrees ('That's a good idea…').

questions.prompt: How many pieces of advice from grandmothers are in the story?
questions.passage:
Grandmothers are full of good advice. They can't resist any opportunity to tell the younger generation 'Sit up straight' or 'Don't put your elbows on the table' or 'If you're nice to them, they'll be nice to you.'

Thinking back to the times she spent with her grandmother, Pauline could remember her only ever giving one piece of advice. When she was a child, she had often stayed with her grandparents and she had to eat food that she didn't have at home. This was when Gran offered her advice. It was 'If you don't try it, you'll never know if you like it.' She had to eat black pudding because Granddad liked it.

Once, Gran had put mushrooms and broccoli in the macaroni cheese because the vegetables needed to be used up. Pauline had shut her eyes and eaten a mouthful. To her surprise it tasted alright. It wasn't something she'd want to eat every day, but it wasn't horrible.

Now, although those times were long behind her and Pauline was travelling the world, Gran's words came back to her. She was sitting cross-legged on the ground in a village in East Africa, looking at the dish of fried scorpions on her knees. Smiling at her hosts, she lifted one to her mouth.
questions.markingGuide: Accept 4. Three general grandmother sayings plus Gran's advice: 'If you don't try it, you'll never know if you like it.'
